title: HelioForge — Channel & Technical Framing
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and HelioForge focused on channel partnership model, technical integration patterns for hybrid GPU onramp, SSO/KMS/security requirements, and pilot success criteria. Redwood AE/SE outlined Dedicated, Private and routing/fallback options; HelioForge shared go-to-market expectations and target customers. Agreed to run a joint pilot with a single PoC customer and exchange security docs and perf benchmark template.
action_items: Maya Chen - send partner one-pager, pricing matrix, and Partner Program overview by 2028-11-10
Ethan Lopez - share perf benchmark template + latency/cost spreadsheet by 2028-11-12
Nina Park (HelioForge) - provide SOC2 attestation contacts and SSO requirements doc by 2028-11-14
Samir Das (HelioForge) - identify PoC customer and their infra constraints by 2028-11-17
next_steps: Schedule technical deep-dive with HelioForge engineering (SE-led) — target week of 2028-11-20
Share Private deployment runbook and VPC subnet checklist
Agree on pilot customer and initial dataset/workload for benchmarks
Set up shared Slack channel and Confluence space; link to partner deck and bench spreadsheet
meeting_header:
Date: 2028-11-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Lopez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Alex Rivera, Samir Das, Renee Holt, Nina Park (HelioForge)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Alex (HelioForge): yeah hi i'm alex, head of partnerships at helioforge, excited to explore how we can resell/onramp redwood to our enterprise customers.
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood): great, i'm ethan on the solutions team, i focus on private and dedicated deployments, latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:24] Priya (Redwood): priya here, i work on the runtime integrations and gpu orchestration.
[00:29] Samir (HelioForge): samir, principal architect, i'll be the technical lead if we do a pilot. we run a mix of on-prem and cloud customers, some air-gapped.
[00:36] Renee (HelioForge): renee, channel ops — i'll handle contracting and pricing discussions.
[00:40] Nina (HelioForge): nina, security lead — i'll review compliance, sso, kms, and audit log needs.
[00:46] Maya: excellent. quick agenda: one, partner model and GTM alignment; two, technical patterns — vpc/private vs dedicated, how routing and fallbacks work; three, pilot scope and next steps. ok?
[00:58] Alex: sounds good. to frame, our customers are fintech and medtech mid-market — they require strict controls and often need private deployments. we also want to bundle an onramp offering that includes GPU capacity from our marketplace.
[01:12] Maya: perfect, that aligns well. redwood offers three deployment modes — hosted api, redwood dedicated for reserved gpu capacity, and redwood private which can be deployed in a customer's vpc or on-prem. ethan? do you want to add a quick note on differences?
[01:28] Ethan: yeah, hosted is easiest but not always acceptable for regulated workloads. dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation — it's our managed reserved pool — and private gives you the most control: customer-managed networking, kms integrations. one note, the private control plane still talks to our control plane for telemetry unless you opt for air-gapped, which is an extra packaging option.
[01:49] Samir: that telemetry piece — for a couple of customers we can't have outbound telemetry. you mentioned air-gap packaging, what's the lift there?
[01:57] Priya: air-gap is heavier — we ship a bundle that includes the control plane components and the runtime. it requires a few static ips and a one-time onboarding. infra-wise we need access to an internal registry or we can push images via secure scp, but support windows higher SLA onboarding costs.
[02:17] Alex: ok good to know. next, from a channel economics view — how do you handle reseller margins and partner billing? is there a partner portal?
[02:27] Maya: we have a Partner Program. typical model: channel discount tiering based on commit and co-sell activity. billing can be consolidated or passed through — we support reseller invoicing if you have a market place. we'll send the one-pager with tiers. renee, would you like a deeper ops doc?
[02:41] Renee: yes please — and examples of committed vs on-demand pricing.
[02:45] Maya: noted.
[02:47] Nina: on security, can you summarize encryption and key management? 
[02:51] Ethan: data in transit is TLS, at-rest encryption uses customer-managed KMS for Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys too if you bring an HSM integration. audit logs are available and can be shipped to a customer SIEM. we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[03:08] Nina: good. also need SAML/SSO and RBAC for partner/ops users.
[03:13] Priya: SSO is supported out-of-the-box, SAML v2.0, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and fine-grained roles in the console.
[03:22] Samir: operationally, we're concerned about routing — if we onboard customers through helioforge marketplace, can traffic be routed to our pools first and fall back to redwood hosted when capacity hits limits?
[03:34] Ethan: yes — we have smart routing policy. you can set priority to route to partner-owned dedicated pools, then to region-hosted pools, then fall back to smaller quantized models to preserve availability. the runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching to keep latency low, though sometimes you'll see a cold-start penalty on first requests.
[03:57] Alex: when you say smaller quantized models, are there quality regressions we need to call out to customers?
[04:03] Priya: there can be slight differences; we ship profile recommendations — e.g., quantized int8 variants are great for chat and embeddings where a small quality delta is acceptable. for high accuracy tasks we recommend pinned fp16 variants. we'll provide a compatibility table.
[04:18] Samir: can we run on our internal k8s, or do you require a specific runtime node image?
[04:24] Priya: the runtime is containerized, we support k8s with gpu plugins (nvidia/container-toolkit), and we can provide helm charts. for air-gapped on-prem we provide the same images but need them uploaded to your registry.
[04:37] Alex: pricing sensitivity — our channel customers ask for per-token cost comparables. can you share typical numbers for embeddings and chat at three latency tiers?
[04:47] Maya: yes, we'll include a pricing matrix and typical per-token benchmarks. ethan will send an example latency/cost spreadsheet.
[04:54] Ethan: i'll also include a model selection recommendation per workload so you can see tradeoffs.
[04:59] Renee: from contracting — SLAs, support tiers, and leakage terms are important. do you do revenue share or fixed margin?
[05:08] Maya: both are possible. early partners usually start with revenue share to bootstrap, then move to committed margins when they have steady demand. we'll include templates.
[05:17] Nina: on compliance — aside from SOC2, do you support customer-managed audit trails and e-discovery for requests?
[05:24] Ethan: we export audit trails; you can route logs to your SIEM and we can hold retention per customer policy. e-discovery is possible through our logs export.
[05:33] Samir: demo request — can we get a performance run against a real customer dataset? we want to see latency p95 for 1k token prompt in our region with our quantization choices.
[05:44] Priya: absolutely — that's what we suggest for pilots. we'll provide a benchmark harness and a runbook. you'll need to provide a sanitized sample dataset and expected prompt mix.
[05:54] Alex: timeline — ideally we'd have a pilot in mid-december to show to two customers for Q1 deals. is that feasible?
[06:02] Maya: yes, if we move quickly on security docs and pick a PoC customer we can target an onboarding in 3–4 weeks.
[06:09] Nina: i'll share SSO requirements and a contact for our compliance officer.
[06:13] Samir: i'll look at candidate customers and confirm infra constraints.
[06:18] Maya: recap then — we will: 1) send partner one-pager and pricing; 2) ethan to send perf benchmark template; 3) helioforge to share security contacts and pick PoC; 4) schedule se-led deep-dive week of 2028-11-20. anyone want to tweak?
[06:34] Alex: sounds right. one ask — can you add an appendix of models you support and quantization options? customers ask.
[06:40] Priya: yes, we'll include a short matrix and links to model profiles. note: some model names may be slightly different in the doc, there's occasionally a mismatch between the internal name and the public model handle.
[06:51] Ethan: i'll also flag any known incompatibilities for on-prem accelerators like older A100 drivers.
[06:58] Renee: contracting — i'll set up a separate thread with our procurement team.
[07:03] Maya: perfect — we'll follow up with the artifacts and link to a shared drive. thanks everyone.
[07:08] Alex: thank you, appreciate it.
[07:10] [End of recording]
notes: Occasional transcription errors present (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache'; 'air-gap' sometimes transcribed as 'area gap'). Multiple references to shared artifacts: partner deck (link to be sent), perf spreadsheet, benchmark harness. Recommended next step: 1) SE deep-dive; 2) pilot runbook; 3) security docs exchange.
